passages.note: Taylor criticizes the bill's 300-foot buffer and $500 fine and says the focus should be on housing the unhoused, which shows opposition to the criminal-penalty approach but not support for any specific one of the remaining rungs.

rows.reasoning: The only passage is a news article quoting Sen. Taylor's own words opposing the camping-ban bill's 300-foot radius provision and $500 fine, arguing government should instead find housing for the unhoused; this establishes opposition to criminal penalties but does not commit to a specific one of the remaining rungs (no penalties of any kind, decriminalizing, or enforcement only when shelter beds are available), so it is direction-only.

quotes.text: What I think we should be working on is finding a place for the unhoused to be housed. This is a bill that looks for a place for the unhoused to remain unhoused, because you can actually move 300 feet and not violate this law.
